- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns bullish (≥0.6) mid-horizon, model frequently fails to sustain upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% incremental lift to later days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility or sentiment swings, apply a 1–2% upward bias toward mid-range historical mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early days (1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 0.5–1.5% to align with true early trend.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ days ≤0.2), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
